8. He submits that from charge-sheet it appears that SI Alam Sarker as investigation officer submitted charge-sheet after conclusion of the investigation of the case and he was made CS witnesses No. 16. In every criminal case, specially murder case, investigation officer always is considered as vital witness. Non-examination of investigation officer operates to the prejudice of the defence as defence gets no chance to cross-examine the investigation officer on various aspects of investigation. He submits that due to absence of the appellants during trial state defence lawyer was appointed. In the absence of the appellants State defence lawyer was there to defend the interest of the defence. Said State defence lawyer got no chance to cross-examine the investigation officer due to his non production as witness at the trial on various appeals of the investigation such as seizure of alamats including the torchlight, preparation of Map and Index of the place of occurrence and other connecting important matters connected with the investigation. As a result defence was highly prejudiced by non-production of investigation officer being vital witness of the case. According to him, it will create benefit for the appellants as to presumption under section 114G, Evidence Act. 

 10. Learned Assistant Attorney-General for the State-respondent submits that occurrence took place at 10-00 PM in the night following 16-12-1990. He shows from first information report Exhibit 1 as well as from evidence of PW 1 that soon after occurrence injured Azizul Islam was first taken to Trisal Health Complex wherefrom he was taken to Mymensingh Medical College Hospital wherein he died in the night of 16-12-1990. He shows that after inquest the dead body was sent for PM examination and after PM examination dead body was taken home for burial. Thereafter first information report was lodged on 19-12-1990 at 19-50 hours by the informant (PW 1). He submits that the delay occurred due to above circumstances cannot be inordinate to create any doubt as to the prosecution story. Learned Assistant Attorney-General shows from record that CS was filed showing the accused absconding. They surrendered to the court and obtained bail therefrom. But subsequently, remained absent and absconding without any reason. State defence lawyer was appointed to defend the absent and absconding accused. He argues that being quite aware of the case against them they remained absent and absconding even till conclusion of trial and pronouncement of judgment by the court. Long absence and absconsion with guilty mind and knowledge about the proceeding against them strong presumption can be taken against the appellants. 

 11. Learned Assistant Attorney-General submits that he finds no reason or explanation in the record from prosecution as to why only means of recognition being the torch of informant was not seized during investigation and not even produced as alamat to be marked Mat Exhibit at the trial in order to prove the story of recognition of the accused during occurrence. He also finds no reason why investigation officer being the vital witness of the case was withheld without explanation. But he submits that since State defence lawyer acted to safeguard the interest of the defence and cross- examined PWs on behalf of defence question of prejudice to be suffered by defence will not arise. He of course admits that seizure list Map and Index prepared by investigation officer could not be proved and marked at the trial due to non-examination of investigation officer or any police officer in such regard. He refers to Exhibit 2 and evidence of PW 2 doctor and contends that manner of occurrence as to overt act of accused-appellants causing injuries to victim Azizul Islam, evidence of PW 1 and other public witnesses duly got corroboration from Exhibit 2 and evidence of PW 2. He finally submits that impugned judgment and order of conviction by court below against appellants having no illegality can have no scope for interference in this appeal which must fail having no merit. We have considered the contentions of both sides and also perused the evidence on record. It appears that CS witness No. 5, 7, 8, 11, 13, 14 and 16 (being investigation officer) were withheld by prosecution at the trial without any reasonable explanation. It will bring presumption under section 114G, Evidence Act. 

 14. It appears that accused remained absent and absconding during trial of the case. State defence lawyer was appointed for the absent accused State defence lawyer cross-examined PWs examined by prosecution. In same way State defence lawyer could not also cross-examine the investigation officer on various aspects of investigation works, specially about seizure of alamats by seizure, preparation of Map and Index of the place of occurrence and also about non-seizure of the torchlight of PW 1 being the only means of recognition of the accused in the darkness of night during occurrence. State defence lawyer was obviously deprived of such scope to cross-examine investigation officer on all about vital aspects of investigation and it is obvious that defence was in above manner prejudiced seriously due to non-examination of the investigation officer. Prosecution offered no explanation as to non-examination of some CS witnesses including investigation officer and it will give rise to presumption under section 114G Evidence Act.
